wu: Superlative Speed Dating: Students stand in two lines, facing each other. They have 30 seconds to ask and answer a superlative question (e.g., 'What's the best movie you've ever seen?'). Then one line moves, and they repeat with a new partner. The teacher calls out topics like 'books', 'food', or 'Ramadan memories'.
wuAlt: Superlative Bingo: Students write 9 superlative questions in a grid. They walk around asking classmates the questions; if a classmate answers 'yes', they can mark the square. The first to get 3 in a row wins.
Find Someone Who...: Students get a handout with prompts like 'Find someone who has read the longest book'. They must ask 'Have you ever read a book longer than 300 pages?' and write down the name.
pres: Teacher shows a 'Class Awards' poster with superlatives like 'The Kindest Heart' and 'The Most Creative Mind'. Models sentences: 'You are the most creative person I've ever met.' and 'This is the best project I've ever seen.' Students repeat. Teacher checks understanding by asking, 'What superlative describes someone who helps everyone?'
presAlt: Award Nomination Box: Students write anonymous nominations on paper slips using superlatives (e.g., 'The funniest joke I've ever heard'). Teacher reads them aloud, and students guess who it is.
Superlative Charades: Teacher acts out a superlative (e.g., 'the tallest') and students guess the word. Then students take turns acting out superlatives like 'the fastest' or 'the most helpful'.
prac: Awards Committee: Students work in groups of 3. Each group gets a set of award cards (e.g., 'Best Dressed', 'Best Storyteller'). They take turns nominating classmates using superlatives: 'I think Sarah is the best storyteller because she tells the funniest stories.' Teacher circulates to correct grammar.
pracAlt: Superlative Chain Game: Students sit in a circle. The first student says a superlative about themselves (e.g., 'I'm the tallest'). The next student must say a superlative about the first student (e.g., 'She's the tallest') and add one about themselves (e.g., 'I'm the fastest').

Nomination Relay: Two teams race to write superlative nominations on the board. The teacher calls out a category (e.g., 'Ramadan kindness'), and the first team to write a correct sentence (e.g., 'You are the most generous person I know') gets a point.
ls: Awards Speech Listening: Students listen to a 2-minute audio of a teacher giving mock awards. They fill in a worksheet with missing superlatives (e.g., 'You are the ___ student I've ever taught'). After, they discuss which award they would give and why.
re: Superlative Freeze: Play music. Students walk around the room. When the music stops, the teacher calls out a superlative (e.g., 'Freeze if you've ever visited a mosque during Ramadan!'). Students who can say 'I've ever visited...' stay in the game. Others sit down.
prod: Class Awards Ceremony: Students work in groups to prepare a 3-minute presentation. They create a poster with 3-4 fun awards (e.g., 'The Best Ramadan Cookie Baker'). Each group presents, explaining why they chose each winner using superlatives: 'We chose Ali because he made the most delicious cookies I've ever tasted!'
rw: Ramadan Guide Writing: Students write a short guide for foreign visitors during Ramadan. They include 6 tips using superlatives (e.g., 'The most important rule is to respect fasting hours'). They also write a paragraph about their favorite Ramadan memory using 'ever' (e.g., 'The best iftar I've ever had was with my family last year').
st: Teacher reads a short story about a boy who wins a 'Most Helpful' award during Ramadan. After, students share one kind thing they've done this week. Close with: 'Today we gave awards using superlatives. Great work! Thank you, class.'
g: Students draw a superlive (e.g., 'the tallest') and their team guesses.
Students write clues about a classmate using superlatives; others guess who it is.
Teams race to write superlative sentences on the board.
Students act out a superlative award and others guess.
Students mark squares when they hear a superlative about Ramadan.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a 'Superlative Trophy' for the class winner, including a reason why they deserve it using 'ever'.
Support learners: Use a sentence frame: 'You are the ___. I've ever seen because ___.'
hw: Record a 90-second video giving a mock award to a classmate, using at least 3 superlatives.
Write 5 more tips for Ramadan visitors, using superlatives like 'the most respectful' or 'the best time'.
Interview a family member about their favorite Ramadan memory and write it down using 'ever'.
tip: Use real examples from the classroom (e.g., 'You are the most creative artist I've seen') to make the language personal and memorable. Connect superlatives to Ramadan values like generosity and community.
